title: Subtraction (up to 20)
description: Class 1 IMO — Subtraction up to 20: taking away, counting back, subtraction facts and word problems, with olympiad reasoning and everyday-maths practice.

topics.title: Taking Away and Counting Back
topics.concept:
Subtraction means taking some away to find how many are left. We use the sign − (minus).

One easy way is to count back. To find 8 − 3, start at 8 and count back three: 7, 6, 5. So 8 − 3 = 5.
recap: Subtraction (−) takes away to find what is left.
The bigger number comes first in 'take away'.

topics.title: Subtraction Facts: Take Away Zero and All
topics.concept:
If you take away zero, nothing changes: 6 − 0 = 6.

If you take away all of a number from itself, you get 0: 7 − 7 = 0. Subtraction is the opposite of addition: since 4 + 3 = 7, we know 7 − 3 = 4.

examples.solution: Taking away zero changes nothing, so 8 − 0 = 8.
Taking away all of it leaves nothing, so 5 − 5 = 0.

recap: Take away 0 → the number stays the same.
Take away the whole number → you get 0.

quiz.explanation: Taking away zero keeps it the same: 10 − 0 = 10.
Taking away all of it leaves 0.

topics.title: Subtraction Word Problems
topics.concept: We subtract to find how many are left or how many more. Words like left, remain, fewer and how many more tell us to subtract.

examples.problem: Meera had 10 sweets. She ate 4. How many are left?
There are 8 birds. 3 fly away. How many remain?

recap: Start with the total and take away.

quiz.q: Aarav had 9 toffees and gave away 5. How many are left?
A jar had 15 biscuits. 6 were eaten. How many remain?

questions.q: There are 12 mangoes. 5 are sold. How many are left?
Riya has 8 pencils, Aarav has 5. How many more does Riya have?
A bus had 16 people. 7 got off. How many are left on the bus?
I take 6 away from a number and get 4. What is the number?
Meera had 20 stickers. She gave 8 to a friend and lost 2. How many are left?
